evals.prompt: I want to add a new skill to skilldrop called `sla-credit-calculator`. It takes a customer contract's SLA terms plus a month of uptime data and outputs the service credit owed, with the calculation shown. It belongs in the sre-oncall pack, it generates an artifact (not a gate), it relates to runbook-generator and incident-comms, and it needs no external deps. Generate everything I need to submit it.
assertions: Produces manifest.json, SKILL.md, evals/cases.json, and a skill-catalogue row, each in its own fenced code block, in a single response
The manifest includes every required field (name, version, description, entrypoint, deps, env, related, tags, model with tier and rationale)
The related array lists only skills that exist (runbook-generator, incident-comms) and tells the author to check the skills directory before finalizing
SKILL.md's How to respond steps are observable actions — none read 'think about X' or 'consider Y'
The quality bar names at least two things the output must never do (e.g. never invent uptime figures not in the input)
evals/cases.json has eight cases with realistic triggers, covering happy-path, edge, anti-pattern, and boundary cases
Ends with next steps that place files under packs/sre-oncall/skills/sla-credit-calculator/ and require python3 validate.py to pass before opening a PR
Does not invent inputs, deps, or related skills the author did not give

evals.prompt: I want to add a skill to our team's skills repo. The repo is this folder (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, existing skills under skills/). The new one is carrier-invoice-audit: you give it a carrier's freight invoice and the rate confirmation for that load, and it lists every line where the carrier billed more than we agreed, with the difference. Ignore differences of $5.00 or less per line. It goes under billing. Related skills are rate-con-extractor and bol-parser. And if it finds a detention charge on the invoice it should kick off detention-claim-letter automatically at the end. Write everything I need for the pull request.
assertions: The skill is delivered as skills/carrier-invoice-audit/ containing skill.yaml, INSTRUCTIONS.md and tests/cases.yaml, the layout CONTRIBUTING.md requires, and not as some other layout such as manifest.json plus SKILL.md
The related list contains rate-con-extractor and does not contain bol-parser, and the reply says bol-parser is not a skill in the repo
The skill's instructions do not make it run or hand off to detention-claim-letter, and the reply says the repo's rule that a skill never calls another skill is the reason
The owner field is a team that appears in OWNERS.md (billing-ops, dispatch or claims), and the reply tells the author the owner was not given and needs confirming
tests/cases.yaml has at least five cases, one of which covers a missing input such as no rate confirmation supplied, following AGENTS.md's rule over the three cases CONTRIBUTING.md asks for
The $5.00 per-line tolerance appears as an exact figure in INSTRUCTIONS.md, and no other threshold or percentage is introduced
A CATALOG.md row for carrier-invoice-audit is provided for the billing table
The reply tells the author to run make check before opening the pull request

evals.prompt: need a new skill for our skills repo. takes the standup notes people paste from slack during the week and writes the friday update that goes to our director. not sure on the name yet, weekly-digest or friday-rollup. Priya wanted it to pull ticket status from Jira too but we don't have API access sorted so leave that out for now i guess. don't know which folder it should live in, whoever set the repo up is on leave. can you write the skill up plus a few test cases so i can open a PR when she's back
assertions: It delivers a drafted instruction file for the skill and at least three test cases, and does not stop at a list of questions
It says the repo's conventions (required files, metadata format or folder) were not available and that the file layout used is an assumption to check
It uses one name for the skill throughout and tells the author the choice between weekly-digest and friday-rollup is still theirs to make
The skill as written does not fetch from Jira and declares no Jira credential, API key or dependency; Jira is mentioned only as left out for now
The skill's instructions tell it to report only what is in the pasted standup notes and not to add progress, blockers or ticket status the notes do not contain
It does not invent the director's name, the team's name, team members other than Priya, or a specific repo folder stated as fact
The test cases use realistic pasted standup notes as input, and at least one covers thin or missing notes
